All four products featured here are available through the Paceline [nutrition and supplements collection](https://paceline.fit/collections/nutrition-supplements), which stocks curated wellness brands and rotates flash sales and seasonal offers throughout the year. Paceline is a health and wellness platform that combines fitness tracking, personalized goals, and a Health Score to give members a clearer picture of their overall wellness — not just steps or workouts. The Paceline+ subscription adds features like personalized goal-setting and Badges that mark meaningful health milestones, alongside access to the marketplace. Supplement savings through the platform are a practical side benefit of an ecosystem designed around long-term health habits.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the best protein powder for muscle gain in 2026?

Whey protein isolate remains the most research-supported option for muscle gain due to its complete amino acid profile and high leucine content. KAGED Whey Protein Isolate and Momentous Whey Protein Isolate are both strong choices, certified by third-party testers for label accuracy and purity.

### Is plant protein as effective as whey for building muscle?

Yes, when plant proteins are blended to cover the full essential amino acid spectrum — particularly pea and rice combinations — research shows outcomes comparable to whey when total daily protein intake is the same. Products like Momentous 100% Plant Protein are formulated with this in mind.

### How do I know if a protein powder is high quality?

The most reliable indicators are third-party certifications such as NSF Certified for Sport or Informed Sport, a clearly labeled amino acid breakdown, and a short ingredient list without excessive fillers or undisclosed proprietary blends.

### How much protein powder should I take per day?

Most active adults benefit from 1.6 to 2.2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight daily, split across meals. One to two scoops of protein powder per day is typical, depending on how much protein is obtained from whole food sources.

### What is the difference between whey isolate and whey concentrate?

Whey isolate is processed further to remove most of the fat and lactose, resulting in a higher protein percentage per gram — typically 90 percent or more. Whey concentrate retains more naturally occurring fats and carbohydrates and is generally less expensive but may cause issues for those sensitive to lactose.

Protein powder is my secret ingredient. The best protein powders are an easy boost to any of your go-to recipes, from smoothies to muffins to morning waffles. I rely on it to fill in the nutritional gaps when [my meals](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-meal-kit-services/) aren’t winning any wellness awards. While the recommended daily allowance for protein is just [0.36 grams per pound of body weight](https://www.health.harvard.edu/blog/how-much-protein-do-you-need-every-day-201506188096#:~:text=The%20Recommended%20Dietary%20Allowance%20(RDA,meet%20your%20basic%20nutritional%20requirements.), that’s the minimum to avoid deficiency, not the sweet spot for optimal health. Depending on how active you are or your dietary needs, [your daily protein recommendation](https://www.nal.usda.gov/human-nutrition-and-food-safety/dri-calculator) may increase. For more on this, check out [How Much Protein Do I Need?](https://www.wired.com/story/how-much-protein-do-i-need/)

Protein powders were once the territory of gym bros trying to bulk up, but the category has since exploded into the mainstream. The powders are now marketed to everyone and available widely, in every form and flavor, and for every dietary preference. Whether you’re [plant-based](https://www.wired.com/story/does-taking-part-in-veganuary-put-people-off-meat-in-the-long-term-heres-what-the-evidence-shows/), a picky eater, or need a quick nutrient boost, protein powder is your fast pass. But with so many options, fads, and a never-ending list of additives, it’s easy to grab the wrong one for your needs. I’ve sifted through the market to find the best of the best protein powder. (As with any dietary supplement, please consult a medical professional or registered dietitian before consuming protein powder.)

For more [powders, tonics, and elixirs](https://www.wired.com/tag/powders-tonics-and-elixirs/), check out our guides to the [Best Protein Bars](https://www.wired.com/story/best-protein-bars/), [Creatine Supplements](https://www.wired.com/story/what-is-creatine/), and [Magnesium Supplements](https://www.wired.com/story/what-are-magnesium-supplements-good-for/).

How I Test Protein Powders

Photograph: Boutayna Chokrane

I've been downing protein powders for years, but for this guide, I put each one through a fresh round of testing. **I sampled each powder at least three times** to assess **taste, texture, and mixability**. I mixed the powders with water, milk, and non-dairy alternatives. I also baked them into muffins and blended them into the occasional smoothie because not all of us like our protein straight.

I prioritized powders with **minimal to no additives** and full transparency in sourcing—no unnecessary fillers, gums, or questionable sweeteners. **Solubility** was a major consideration, too. I also scrutinized **manufacturing practices** and **third-party testing. Certifications,** like NSF Certified for Sport or Informed Choice, mattered (learn more about these [below](#factors)). Every pick is also a **complete protein**, meaning it contains all nine essential amino acids.

  Optimum Nutrition’s Gold Standard Whey has been a longtime favorite among gym rats. It’s affordable, widely available, and the flavors we’ve tested taste good. The powder delivers 24 grams of protein per serving and is sourced from a blend of whey isolate, concentrate, and peptides. The vanilla ice cream flavor has been my go-to for three years. I use it in smoothies, but I love it even more for baking. I like to swap a couple of scoops for some of the flour in banana bread to give it a protein boost without tasting chalky. Reviewer Louryn Strampe loves [the banana cream](https://cna.st/affiliate-) flavor, which she swears tastes like a yellow Laffy Taffy. While the sheer number of flavor options is nice, know that some flavors include artificial sweeteners.

  While there are protein powders out there with fewer additives, it’s reassuring to know the Clean Label Project gave the vanilla ice cream flavor its [stamp of approval](https://cleanlabelproject.org/protein-study-2-0/) last year, confirming it tested free of arsenic, lead, cadmium, and mercury.

  Note: [Consumer Reports found](https://www.consumerreports.org/lead/protein-powders-and-shakes-contain-high-levels-of-lead-a4206364640/) that while certain Optimum Nutrition Powders are safe for regular use, the brand's [Serious Mass](https://cna.st/affiliate-) contained 8.5 micrograms of inorganic arsenic per serving, which is twice the amount deemed safe by experts.

**[Naked Casein](https://cna.st/affiliate-):** With only one ingredient—micellar casein sourced from hormone-free skim milk—this is about as clean as it gets. No added sugar, no artificial sweeteners, and no unnecessary additives. It's cold-processed to avoid any nastiness from chemicals or synthetic fillers, and it’s independently tested for both heavy metals and gluten. Each serving packs 26 grams of protein and 618 milligrams of calcium (about 48 percent of your daily value). But Naked Casein doesn’t contain the emulsifying lecithin, so it won’t dissolve as smoothly as other powders. The best way to mix is with a blender, but I couldn't stomach the taste of this one.

**[Ghost Whey Protein Powder](https://cna.st/affiliate-):** Ghost is the protein powder for people who want their post-workout snack to taste like dessert. With flavors like Trix, Cinnabon, and coffee ice cream, it's unsurprisingly one of the best-tasting whey proteins on the market. Each scoop delivers 25 grams of protein (nearly 50 percent of the daily value for many people) and blends well in shakes, oats, or even DIY protein ice cream. The trade-off here is a longer ingredient list that includes gums, high-fructose corn syrup, and—in some flavors—titanium dioxide, which is a whitening pigment banned as a food additive in Europe.

**[Seeq Clear Protein Powder](https://cna.st/affiliate-):** At first, I was skeptical of Seeq Clear Protein (how could it be clear!?!), but I’m a sucker for anything watermelon-flavored. I was pleasantly surprised. It tastes like a creamier sports drink (I promise it’s better than that description sounds), and each serving has 22 grams of protein and 4.5 grams of BCAAs. Its protein blend includes whey concentrate, casein, milk protein isolate, whey protein isolate, hydrolyzed whey isolate, and micellar casein, so you get a mix of fast and slow-digesting proteins. It also delivers 450 milligrams of calcium and 880 milligrams of potassium, which is a bonus if you want to squeeze in some micronutrients. It tastes great—the strawberry milkshake flavor is spot-on—but these are two scoops at 310 grams, so you'll need to be comfortable with the jumbo serving size. I can't fully endorse the formula because it's packed with artificial sweeteners like sucralose and acesulfame potassium, as well as some iffy additives, including maltodextrin and a gum blend (cellulose, guar, gum Arabic, and xanthan) that might not sit well with everyone. Courtesy of Amazon

It’s USDA-certified organic, kosher, and delivers 21 grams of protein per serving, plus 4 grams of fiber and prebiotics for a little digestive support. It leans higher in carbs than some plant-based competitors at about 15 grams per serving, but that also makes it more filling—ideal if you need something to hold you over between meals. I’ve tested my fair share of vanilla proteins, and Orgain’s vanilla bean flavor is one of the better ones available. It’s smooth, not overly sweet, and blends up surprisingly creamy despite being dairy-free. While the formula is free from artificial sweeteners, most flavors include erythritol and gums, which can cause digestive issues for some. Certain flavors, like [birthday cake](https://cna.st/affiliate-), sneak up to 450 milligrams of sodium per serving, which is 20 percent of your daily limit. The [iced coffee flavor](https://cna.st/affiliate-) comes with 60 milligrams of caffeine.

**[Aloha 12oz Chocolate Sea Salt Protein Drink (Pack of 12)](https://cna.st/affiliate-):** Aloha's protein powder is still on my testing docket, but I have tried the brand's ready-to-drink shakes. The chocolate sea salt is surprisingly tasty; it's creamy and rich, but there's a faint aftertaste. I sometimes use the vanilla flavor as a milk base for smoothies, and there's also a coconut flavor I haven't gotten my hands on yet. Each serving packs 18 grams of plant-based protein.

## Avoid These

Last October, Consumer Reports (CR) [tested](https://www.consumerreports.org/lead/protein-powders-and-shakes-contain-high-levels-of-lead-a4206364640/) 23 popular protein powders and ready-to-drink shakes and found that more than two-thirds of the products contained more lead in a single serving than what the publication considers safe to consume in a day. CR's level of concern for lead is 0.5 micrograms per day, which is based on [California’s Prop 65](https://oehha.ca.gov/proposition-65), a law requiring businesses to inform consumers about exposure to harmful chemicals.

The TL;DR version: Plant-based powders had the highest levels of lead, about nine times more than dairy-based options and twice as much as beef-based powders. Whey and other dairy-derived supplements tended to fare better, but even half of those tested still contained enough lead for CR to caution against daily use.

This WIRED article is a comprehensive review of the best protein powders on the market, tested by author Boutayna Chokrane. The article provides detailed evaluations of top protein powders across various categories, including whey-based, plant-based, and specialty options.

**Top Recommendations:**

1. **Best Overall - Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey Protein Powder** ($45, 31% off): 24g protein per serving, available in 12+ flavors, Clean Label Project approved. A versatile, affordable favorite.

2. **Best Whey Isolate - Transparent Labs Grass-Fed Whey Protein Isolate** ($60): 28g protein, 21 flavors, no artificial sweeteners/fillers, Informed Choice certified.

3. **Best Plant-Based - Ritual Protein Daily Shake 18+** ($29, 34% off): 20g protein from organic yellow peas, NSF-certified, Clean Label Project Purity Award winner.

4. **Best Tasting - Dymatize ISO100 Whey Protein Isolate** ($42): 25g protein, 11 flavors including Fruity Pebbles, contains 5.5g BCAAs.

5. **Best for Athletes - Promix Whey Isolate Protein Powder** ($65): 30g protein, grass-fed, micro-filtered (<1g lactose), easy to digest.

6. **Best for Sensitive Stomachs - Momentous Grass Fed Whey Protein Isolate** ($60): 20g protein, European grass-fed dairy, NSF Certified for Sport, no fillers/gums.

7. **Best Low Carb - Isopure Zero Carb** ($90): 25g protein, zero carbs/sugar, 8 flavors, ideal for baking.

8. **Best for Paleo - Be Well by Kelly Chocolate Grass-Fed Beef Protein Powder** ($65): 24g protein, only 3 ingredients (organic cacao, beef protein isolate, monk fruit), dairy-free.

9. **Best for Fiber - Mikuna Vegan Protein Powder** ($44): 20g protein from Peruvian lupin bean (chocho), vegan/paleo/keto/gluten-free, but gritty texture.

10. **Cleanest Protein - Puori PW1 Whey Protein** ($79): 21g protein, Clean Label Project certified, minimal ingredients, pasture-raised non-GMO cows.

**Testing Methodology:** The author sampled each powder at least three times, testing taste, texture, and mixability with water, milk, and non-dairy alternatives. Powders were also baked into muffins and blended into smoothies. Priority was given to powders with minimal additives, full transparency, good solubility, third-party testing, and complete protein profiles.

**Key Concerns:** Consumer Reports testing found that over two-thirds of popular protein powders contained more lead per serving than considered safe for daily consumption. Plant-based powders had the highest lead levels (9x more than dairy-based). The article advises moderation and transparency in sourcing.

**Also Considered:** Naked Casein, Ghost Whey, Seeq Clear Protein, Sakara Protein + Greens, BSN True-Mass Weight Gainer, Orgain Organic Vegan Protein, and Aloha ready-to-drink shakes.

## How we chose the best protein powders

Healthline’s dietitians determined the best protein powders using the following criteria:

* **Ingredient and nutrient quality:** We looked for products that are made from high quality ingredients and contain minimal amounts of added sugars and artificial additives.
* **Quality testing:** We prioritized products that are third-party tested for quality, accuracy, and purity. We also looked for products that are third-party certified to be safe for competitive athletes.
* **Reviews:** The protein powders listed below have either been tried and recommended by Healthline editors or have mostly positive online reviews.
* **Price:** We included options to suit a variety of budgets.

Additionally, every brand and product on our list has been vetted to ensure that it aligns with Healthline’s brand integrity standards and approach to well-being. Each product in this article meets the following criteria:

* **FDA compliance:** All brands and products adhere to allowable health claims and labeling requirements, per Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations. Additionally, products are manufactured in facilities that adhere to the Current Good Manufacturing Practices established by the FDA.
* **Medical and business standards:** Products are produced by medically credible companies that follow ethical, legal, and industry best standards. Companies also provide objective measures of trust, such as having their supplements validated by third-party labs.
* **Health claims:** Products don’t make outlandish health or medical claims, and any claims that are made align with Healthline’s approach to well-being.

## How each type of protein powder works

The type of protein powder you choose depends on your dietary needs, health goals, and personal preferences. Learn about how each type of protein works in the sections below.

* **Whey:** Whey is a milk-based protein that’s quickly and easily digested and absorbed. When combined with resistance training, [whey protein](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/whey-protein-101) may help [increase muscle mass](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36839361/) and support growth, so it’s a great choice for athletes.
* **Casein:** [Casein](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/what-is-casein) is a protein in milk that’s [digested and absorbed slowly](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7468913/), which can help you feel full longer, so it may help reduce your appetite. The slower digestion and absorption rate [may also support](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32698256/) muscle growth and recovery over longer periods.
* **Egg white:** [Egg white protein](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/egg-whites-nutrition) is a great alternative to whey or casein protein, especially for people with an allergy to dairy products.
* **Collagen powder:** [Collagen](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/collagen) is a component of muscles, and supplementing with it may have benefits for [bone and joint](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39980497/) health. However, collagen is not a complete protein and doesn’t build and repair muscles optimally like other sources of protein, such as whey, pea, and egg.
* **Plant-based protein:** People following a vegan lifestyle [should opt](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6643/13/6/1962) for plant-based protein sources, such as pea or brown rice. [Vegan protein powders](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/best-vegan-protein-powder-review) can also be suitable for people who follow a dairy-free diet or have trouble digesting dairy or lactose.

### Concentrate vs. isolate vs. hydrolysate

Whey protein, in particular, is available in concentrate, isolate, or hydrolysate form, although many supplements contain a combination of the three.

Although whey concentrate and isolate offer similar benefits, whey protein isolate undergoes processing methods that result in a higher concentration of protein and lower amounts of fat, carbs, and lactose.

Meanwhile, whey hydrolysate, or hydrolyzed whey, has been [partially broken down](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31095313/) to ease digestion and speed absorption.

## How to choose a protein powder

### Key factors to consider

* **Protein source:** Protein powders contain either animal-based or plant-based protein sources. Examples of animal-based proteins include [casein](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/casein-protein-is-highly-underrated), whey, [collagen](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/collagen-benefits), and egg. Plant-based protein powders often contain pea, rice, soy, or hemp protein. Some vegan blends also contain whole grains, nuts, and seeds.
* **Additional ingredients:** Look for protein powders that have as few ingredients as possible. Always check the labels carefully, and consider avoiding products containing [artificial sweeteners](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/artificial-sweeteners-good-or-bad), colors, and flavors.
* **Quality testing:** Because the FDA doesn’t evaluate the safety, quality, or effectiveness of protein powders, it’s best to choose products that are third-party tested to ensure purity and potency.
* **“Safe for sport” designation:** Competitive athletes may want to choose a protein powder that has been tested for banned substances by an organization such as [NSF International](https://www.nsfsport.com/) or [Informed Sport](https://sport.wetestyoutrust.com/).
* **Flavors and texture:** Protein powders come in a variety of flavors, and some mix more easily than others. Online reviews, ingredient lists (specifically the type of sweetener[s] used), and single-serving packets can all help with deciding whether a product will suit your palate or not.

## When is the best time to take protein?

The best time to take protein powder depends on your health goals. You may want to have one large portion or several small portions of protein per day.

* **To lose weight:** Try incorporating more high protein foods throughout the day, as [studies show](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7539343/) that increasing your intake of protein could help reduce appetite and cravings.
* **To improve athletic performance or endurance:** [When to consume protein powder](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/protein-shake-before-or-after-workout) largely depends on your overall fitness goals. While research suggests that the amount of protein you consume throughout the day is more important than the timing, many experts still recommend consuming [protein post-training](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40221559/) or post-competition.
* **To build muscle:** It’s generally recommended to consume protein powder [within 2 hours](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28919842/) of a weightlifting session. [Some research](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36857005/) also suggests that taking protein powder before you go to sleep may help your muscles recover overnight. But research shows that daily protein intake is the most important factor in muscle building.
* **To prevent muscle loss:** Focus on eating moderate amounts of protein throughout the day to [help prevent muscle loss](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32232404/) in older adults.

**»Learn more:**[When is the best time to take protein?](https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/best-time-to-take-protein)

## Frequently asked questions about protein powder

Protein powders are generally safe for most adults, but some types can cause [digestive issues](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10079511/) like bloating or cramps, and occasionally [skin reactions](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10969252/).

Lower-quality products may [contain contaminants](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40703701/) (like heavy metals), so choosing a third-party tested brand is important.

If you have a medical condition, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or take medications, it is best to consult a healthcare professional before use.

There are many excellent protein brands, and all of the ones in this article have been vetted carefully by our in-house team.

When looking for protein powder, it is important to check how much protein is in each serving to make sure it meets your needs. It is also a good idea to only purchase from companies that use third-party testing to make sure that the products do not contain harmful ingredients.

[Gainful](https://click.linksynergy.com/deeplink?id=9%2FEdAQ1wkL8&mid=45086&murl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gainful.com%2Fproducts%2Fcollagen-whey-protein%3Fvariant%3D43018698588299%26selling_plan%3D1825964171&rvo_aff=1&rvo_brandid=Gainful&rvo_prodid=f3ef1320-dbea-43f8-9143-21f5c8424045&rvo_subid=f3ef1320-dbea-43f8-9143-21f5c8424045&U1=+correlationId&rvo_subid2=+where) is a great option for beginners, as it creates a custom protein blend based on your dietary needs and fitness goals. What’s more, you can mix and match the Flavor Boosts to find what works for you.

If [gaining muscle mass](/health/fitness/how-to-gain-muscle) is your goal, research suggests choosing a product with [at least 20 g](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28919842/) of high quality protein and minimal fillers, sweeteners, and artificial ingredients.

Though any of the protein powders listed above can support muscle gain when paired with resistance training, [Gainful](https://click.linksynergy.com/deeplink?id=9%2FEdAQ1wkL8&mid=45086&murl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gainful.com%2Fproducts%2Fcollagen-whey-protein%3Fvariant%3D43018698588299%26selling_plan%3D1825964171&rvo_aff=1&rvo_brandid=Gainful&rvo_prodid=f3ef1320-dbea-43f8-9143-21f5c8424045&rvo_subid=f3ef1320-dbea-43f8-9143-21f5c8424045&U1=+correlationId&rvo_subid2=+where) is a particularly great option for its three whey protein options.

Plant-based protein can be a great option for vegans and people who are unable to tolerate dairy. However, whey and plant-based protein powders offer similar health benefits.

For example, [some research](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37810915/) suggests that whey protein and pea-based protein perform similarly in supporting recovery and metabolic responses in athletes, with only minor differences that are not significant enough to justify choosing one type over the other.

## The bottom line

When trying a new protein powder, pay attention to how your body responds. As with any supplement, you may wish to take a break every so often or alternate between different products.

Many people get plenty of protein from the foods they eat.

However, if you’re trying to increase your protein intake, having a protein shake or adding protein powder to foods, like oatmeal and yogurt, can help you meet your needs.

Finally, try to consume plenty of whole, fresh foods, including natural sources of protein and fiber, as well as plenty of water, for a healthy diet.

*    High-Protein Formula to Support Muscle Health – Delivers 24g of fast-absorbing 100% whey protein per scoop to support post-workout muscle recovery, muscle strength and muscle building when taken over time with regular resistance training.

*    Optimized Support for Strength & Hypertrophy Goals – Whey protein isolate is the primary ingredient with excess carbs and fat “isolated” out. Ideal for athletes looking to increase muscle strength or boost recovery between workouts. 
*    Mixes Smoothly for Rapid Post-Workout Use – Instantized powder dissolves quickly in water or milk, making it a convenient shake immediately after training.

7. Summarize lengthy explanations while keeping the core message intact.

When handling different types of content:

- For news articles: Focus on the who, what, when, where, why, and how.

- For opinion pieces: Maintain the main arguments and supporting points.

## Everything You Need To Know

We get it. You’re never satisfied with your last achievement. Today’s finish line is tomorrow’s starting point, and each drop of sweat is a reminder that moving and pushing yourself gets results. You put your body through a lot, and it deserves real nutrition to fuel your personal best. We got you.

Orgain 30g\* Plant Protein Powder in Vanilla flavor delivers all nine essential amino acids (EAAs) and branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) to help stimulate optimal muscle protein growth and to repair and rebuild muscle fibers\*\*\*. This Vanilla flavored Plant Protein Powder is made with our organic fruit and veggie blend as well as tart cherry, turmeric, and ginger, and provides a good source (4g\*) of prebiotic fiber to support digestion.

Orgain 30g\* Plant Protein is USDA-certified organic, non-GMO, made with no soy and gluten free, so you can trust that you’re giving your body the high-quality nutrition it needs. Let’s get real, muscle support shouldn’t have to taste bad or gritty. That’s why Orgain hand selects ingredients to create a smooth, creamy and intensely satisfying taste experience like no other.​

### What types of sweeteners does 30g Plant Protein use?

The 30g Plant Protein Powder is sweetened with organic agave inulin fiber and organic stevia.

### Is 30g Plant Protein Powder a pre-workout or post-workout?

A single serving of 30g Plant Protein Powder provides 9g of essential amino acids (EAAs) and BCAA and can be taken either before or after exercise. It helps support muscle protein synthesis and lean tissue repair. Some individuals prefer consuming pre-workout for added energy and convenience, while others opt for post-workout intake to aid recovery.

### Can I use the 30g Plant Protein Powder as a meal replacement?

Orgain’s 30g Plant Protein Powder on its own is not considered a meal replacement, as meal replacement shakes typically offer a more comprehensive nutritional profile. However, when paired with other nutrient-rich foods, it can contribute to a balanced meal.

### Is there caffeine in the 30g Plant Protein Powder?

There is no caffeine added. The Creamy Chocolate Fudge flavor contains about 7-8mg of naturally occurring caffeine from the organic cocoa. To put that in perspective, an 8 oz cup of coffee contains approximately 95mg of caffeine. We recommend consulting with your healthcare provider to make sure Orgain is right for you.

### How should I store the protein powder?

Please store the protein powder in a dry, cool place, such as a closet or pantry. Do not store the protein powder in the refrigerator or freezer as moisture can shorten the shelf life.

### What is the best way to mix this protein powder?

Mix 2 scoops in 12-16 ounces of water, milk, or liquid of your choice, and shake in a shaker cup or prepare in a blender. To prevent clumping, always be sure to put the liquid into the container first, with the powder added on top.

# Vega Protein Powder Review (2026): Plant-Based Protein That Actually Tastes Good?

![8662](https://i.garagegymreviews.com/114/428/369/7/sydney-lappe-150x150.webp)

Written by Sydney Lappe, R.D.

![8662](https://i.garagegymreviews.com/114/428/369/7/sydney-lappe-150x150.webp)

[Sydney Lappe, R.D.](/author/sydney-lappe)

Sydney Lappe is a St. Louis-based Registered Dietitian with 6+ years of nutrition editing and writing experience. She holds a Master’s Degree in Nutrition and Dietetics and completed undergrad work in psychology. While fitness wasn’t in Sydney’s routine growing up, it quickly became a large part of her daily life while studying the facets of health and nutrition. Also managing chronic pain, she has come to fully realize movement is a special gift to never take for granted and hopes to inspire others to invest in their physical, mental, and emotional wellness while they can. Including her passion for all things health, Sydney enjoys spending time with her loved ones, being active in various capacities, drinking bottomless cups of coffee, eating a hearty bowl of oatmeal, and letting her creativity roam through writing and graphic design.

We test and review fitness products based on an independent, multi-point methodology. If you use our links to purchase something, we may earn a commission. [Read our disclosures](https://www.garagegymreviews.com/disclosure)

Protein powders are on the rise, as a [Global Market Insights](https://www.gminsights.com/industry-analysis/protein-powder-market) (GMI) report tells us that the protein powder market size surpassed $21.5 billion in 2022. Oh, and it’s anticipated to expand at a 6.5% growth rate within the next decade!

Now begs the question: What’s driving such a significant increase? Allow us to reintroduce you to vegan protein powders. Yep, the GMI report hints the protein powder boom is largely due to vegan and plant-based nutrition trends—and that plant-based proteins are picking up pace in the supplement industry, providing many of the same benefits as the [best whey protein powders](/best-whey-protein).

But Vega, a plant-based supplement brand, planted its seed in 2001 and may just be ahead of its “thyme.” In this in-depth Vega protein powder review, find out if and how this plant-based protein can help your health flourish.

*Medical disclaimer: This article is intended for educational and informational purposes only. It is not intended as a substitute for medical advice. For health advice, contact a licensed healthcare provider. GGR also recommends choosing a product that has been third-party tested for quality.*

### We Go Out of Our Whey to Find Inclusive Solutions

If you’re a naturally bred whey protein consumer, you very likely understand that plant-based proteins are, ehh, different. From the taste to the solubility, plant proteins generally just do not provide our senses with the same experience as whey-based options.

But as registered dietitians and nutrition experts, we genuinely understand (and appreciate) that everyone has their own unique dietary needs and preferences. And it’s our job to provide solutions for all—this means happily going out of our way to find inclusive, non-dairy protein options when animal-based products are off the table for whatever reason.

Vega Sport Premium Protein

### [Vega Sport Premium Protein](/equipment/vega-sport-premium-protein "Vega Sport Premium Protein")

[![product image](https://i.garagegymreviews.com/716/651/944/vega-sport-premium-protein.webp)](/equipment/vega-sport-premium-protein)

GGR Score: 4.03

[Check Price](https://www.garagegymreviews.com/go/vega-sport-plant-protein)

### Product Highlights

* Multi-source vegan protein powder
* NSF Certified for Sport, vegan, and gluten-free
* Includes BCAAs, probiotics, and tart cherry

### Pros & Cons

#### Pros

* 30 grams of protein per serving
* Contains all essential amino acids but two that are made by the body
* 5 flavor options
* Supports recovery with tart cherry, probiotics, and turmeric extract

#### Cons

* Customers share new formula doesn’t blend well
* Pricey at over $2 per serving

### Bottom Line

Vega Sport Protein is plant-based, third-party tested, and gluten-free, making it suitable for a wide variety of people. One scoop provides 30 grams of vegan-friendly protein. Our testers report taste and blendability is not comparable to whey protein, but far better than other vegan-friendly options on the market.

## A Quick Look at Vega Sport Protein

Vega Sport Premium is a vegan protein powder created by Vega, a supplement company that is passionate about plants and plant-based nutrition. Really, just one glimpse of Vega’s official website tells you it’s a [B-Corp Certified](https://myvega.com/pages/b-corp) company inspired and motivated by plants with sustainable solutions for people and the planet.

Digging into the website, you’ll also learn that Vega planted its seeds in 2001 by co-founder Brandan Branzie, a vegan triathlete, after being frustrated by the lack of high-performance options. Fast forward to now, Vega continues to expand its nourishing product line to support general wellness and sports performance—oh, and growing trees with every purchase (more on this coming up)!

Overall, Vega is a plant-forward supplement company passionate about the power of plants. And with a unique plant-protein blend, tart cherry powder, and probiotics, Vega Sport may help your workout performance, recovery, gut health, and more.

### Before You Buy

* Vega Sport provides a hearty 30 grams of plant-based protein, contains all essential amino acids, and comes in five flavors, like Berry, Chocolate, and Mocha.
* Being NSF Certified for Sport, plant-based athletes can confidently consume Vega Sport knowing it’s free of banned substances.

## Is Vega Protein Worth It?

Costing a touch over $3.00 per serving on the Vega website, Vega Sport is on the high end compared to other winners on our [best vegan protein powder](/best-vegan-protein-powder) round-up. However, we awarded Vega Sport as the best-tasting—which might even be more impressive than its 30 grams of protein per serving, given the general track record of plant-based proteins and their flavor ratings.

Orrr maybe not as impressive as it being a complete protein! Unlike most plant-based proteins, Vega Sport’s vegan blend provides nine essential amino acids.

So because of its rich protein content and flavor variety, along with its certifications we’ll be sure to touch on, we think Vega Protein might be a worthy option for anyone focusing on a plant-forward diet.

### **Great for:**

* Loose or strict plant-based dieters—such as vegetarians and vegans—searching for a gluten-free, convenient, and complete protein
* Plant-based athletes who want peace of mind knowing that Vega Sport is NSF Certified for Sport
* Anyone looking for a unique protein blend without added sugars, including those managing blood sugars or following a low-carbohydrate or keto diet

### **Not recommended for:**

* Whey-based protein lovers who might not be partial to the uniqueness of plant-based proteins—mixability, especially, is a distinctive factor to get used to
* Plant-based eaters looking for a Certified Organic product
* Those with a delicate and sensitive tummy, mostly due to Vega Sport’s added probiotics

## Formulation

While knowing the cost is important, it’s arguably more important to understand exactly what you’re paying for. Let’s see what each scoop will provide you with.

### Plant-Based Protein

Vega Sport protein provides 30 grams of plant-based protein sourced by:

* **Pea protein****:** Although relatively new to the protein supplement scene, [pea protein](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31429319/)1 has a well-balanced amino acid profile with a high level of lysine. The plant-based protein is a great substitution for animal and soy proteins, and [research](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25628520/)2 shows pea protein can spur muscle growth and be used as an alternative to whey-based dietary products.

* **Pumpkin seed** **protein:** [Pumpkin seed protein](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2468227620303136)3 contains high values of bioavailable amino acids and minerals like potassium, calcium, and iron. It also shows promising antioxidative and chelating properties, which may enhance mineral absorption.

* **Organic** **sunflower seed** **protein:** While mostly known for its fat content, sunflower seeds are a rich source of protein and amino acids. This includes essential amino acids—like phenylalanine, leucine, and methionine—that can only be obtained from [high-protein foods](/high-protein-foods).

* **Alfalfa** **protein:** While often used as animal feed, [alfalfa](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/alfalfa-protein) is considered a green leaf protein source.

Taken together, the blend supplies 5 grams of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs)—specifically 2.56 g of leucine, 1.44 g of isoleucine, and 1.56 g of valine. However, it does not contain the ideal BCAA 2:1:1 ratio like these [best BCAA supplements](/best-bcaa) and the recommended [3 grams of leucine](https://jissn.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1550-2783-9-54)4 to maximize protein synthesis, but it’s quite close.

### Tart Cherry Powder

Vega Sport contains tart cherry powder, which Vega suggests is “the cherry on top of your post-workout recovery plan.” The pun game with this claim is truly cherrific, but we need to dig into the data and not just cherry-pick the facts.

A [2017 review](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318388708_Tart_Cherry_Juice_in_Athletes_A_Literature_Review_and_Commentary)5 tells us that tart cherry provides antioxidant and anti-inflammatory polyphenols. These powerful plant compounds may lessen pain and inflammatory markers while accelerating strength recovery after exercise.

According to a 2015 study published in the [Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26578852/)6*,* resistance-trained men supplementing with 480 milligrams of tart cherry powder near a bout of resistance exercise may attenuate muscle soreness and the breakdown and strength reduction during recovery. A similar [2016 study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27231439/)7 examined the effects of 480 milligrams of tart cherry in endurance-trained individuals and found very similar recovery benefits while improving endurance performance.

But despite the scientific backing of tart cherry, Vega does not indicate how much cherry powder is in the formula. That said, while the tart cherry isn’t likely to cause harm, we can’t fully assume that you’ll reap these claimed benefits without knowing the dose.

### Probiotics

The protein powder provides 2 billion CFUs of probiotics, which are a type of “good” and live bacteria that support gut, brain, immune, and overall health. The [best probiotics](/best-probiotic) have quite a bit of variance in the number of CFUs—ranging from 1 to 100B (!!)—and strains they contain.

Vega Sport protein contains the strain [Bacillus coagulans](https://medlineplus.gov/druginfo/natural/1185.html) (B. coagulans), which is often used to manage constipation, irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and other digestive conditions. The strain is mostly considered safe—including taking 6 billion CFUs daily for up to three months or lower doses for up to one year.

Despite the general safety, different probiotic strains offer different health benefits—like Lactobacillus acidophilus, which also helps reduce IBS symptoms, and Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG, which might improve blood pressure. So if you do have specific health needs and goals, we do recommend selecting a probiotic strain to match.

### Other Ingredients

Already, Vega Sport has a pretty robust ingredient line-up, but there’s more.

* **Natural flavors****:** This is a pretty vague ingredient, as “natural flavors” could be a substance created by a variety of animal and plant sources like spices, fruits and veggies, yeasts, dairy products, and meats. While we can’t exactly pinpoint the specific “natural flavor,” we can at least assume it’s extracted from a plant-based food source and agree it’s better than containing artificial flavors.
* **Sea salt:** [Salt](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0963996909003044)8 helps extract the pea protein while enhancing the flavor of the protein powder.
* **Stevia leaf** **extract:** Vega claims stevia is their favorite sweetener because it’s plant-based without providing calories. They do suggest if you don’t like stevia, and can taste it in the protein powder, to try adding a squirt of lemon juice or blending it with dark leafy greens.
* **Xanthan gum:** Because [xanthan gum](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/xanthan-gum) is used as a stabilizer and is soluble in cold water, it’s often used in plant-based protein powders to provide it with a creamier consistency when mixed. Xanthan gum is mostly considered to be a safe food additive, although it can lead to tummy troubles.
* **Bromelain:** Extracted from pineapples, [bromelain](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1729/11/4/317)9 is a proteolytic enzyme that helps break down protein. It may also benefit various body systems—like digestive, circulatory, and immune systems—and ease arthritis symptoms.
* **Turmeric extract:** Turmeric contains the beneficial component curcumin, which may enhance performance and post-exercise recovery by reducing muscle damage and inflammation according to a [2021 review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32319320/).10 Interestingly, too, bromelain9 shows to significantly improve the absorption of curcumin.
* **Black pepper extract:** Speaking of curcumin absorption, [research](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3535097/)11 suggests the piperine sourced from black pepper increases the bioavailability of curcumin by a whopping 2,000%!

## Side Effects

Plant proteins tend to be isolated from wheat and soybeans, which are part of the nine [common food allergens](https://www.fda.gov/food/food-labeling-nutrition/food-allergies). However, Vega discloses that the protein is manufactured in a facility that also processes peanuts, milk, soy, egg, tree nuts, and sesame, which ultimately poses the risk of cross-contamination.

Other food and ingredient components worthy of side effect callouts include:

* **Sodium:** While flavor-dependent, the pea protein powder-based supplement also provides upwards of 370 milligrams of sodium. While sodium is an important [electrolyte](/best-electrolyte-drink), people with certain medical conditions—like kidney disease and heart failure—might have sodium (and protein) restrictions.
* **Caffeine:** It’s also important to note that the Chocolate and Mocha flavors contain caffeine, although in small amounts. While marginal, some people might be sensitive to caffeine and/or trying to be more intentional about their intake.
* **Alfalfa****:** High doses or long-term intake of alfalfa may increase the symptoms of lupus, multiple sclerosis, and other autoimmune conditions. Also because alfalfa is rich in vitamin K, it can interact with the blood-clotting medication warfarin.

All-in-all, it’s always a smart idea to double-check the ingredients and any potential adverse side effects and interactions, especially if managing a health condition and/or taking medication(s). Consult with a dietitian or another healthcare professional for your utmost safety and benefit.

## Third-Party Testing

Did you know protein powder and other dietary supplements do not have to be approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) before you shake it up and chug it down? That’s why we are always, always checking for third-party testing—testing completed by independent agencies—and encourage consumers to do the same so they know the exterior product label matches its interior contents.

Vega Sport is [NSF Certified for Sport](https://www.nsf.org/consumer-resources/articles/certified-for-sport-program), which lets us know two essential details: One is that what you see on the label is actually what you get. And two, that the protein powder is tested and free of banned substances identified by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), which is particularly important for competitive athletes and their teams.

NSF is also the only independent testing organization to evaluate every detail of the production process. Ongoing and unannounced plant inspections further ensure that the products are compliant with program requirements and high industry standards.

To add, Vega Sport is gluten-free and verified by the Non-GMO Project as well. This means it’s produced without genetic engineering and GMO-derived ingredients.

## Vega Protein Powder Review FAQs

### **Is Vega a good brand for protein powder?**

Based on the high-quality protein formulation and positive customer reviews, Vega (in our opinion) is a great protein powder brand. They also provide a wide variety of products—such as Vega Real Food Smoothie and Vega Protein & Green—to support various health goals and needs.

### **Is Vega protein good for weight loss?**

Because consuming adequate protein is a key factor for weight loss and maintenance, we have awarded Vega Sport as one of the [best protein powders for weight loss](/best-protein-powder-for-weight-loss). However, it’s essential to remember that weight loss requires much more than drinking a protein shake, but it can aid in your efforts.

### **Is Vega better than whey?**

While whey is considered a complete protein, unlike most plant-based sources, Vega possesses a rich amino acid profile that just about anyone can benefit from. If your diet is free of dairy and animal products, we encourage you to vary your protein sources to help ensure you’re consuming all essential amino acids.

### **Is Vega protein powder hard to digest?**

Eh, it depends on the person and their own unique tolerances or lack thereof. But we’ll unpack a few considerations:

**Free of lactose and dairy:** Because Vega is lactose and dairy-free, it might be a viable protein solution for people with lactose-intolerance or dairy sensitivities.   
**Reduced dietary fiber:** Plant-based proteins also tend to be rich in dietary fiber, which plays an essential role for health, although some people may find it hard to digest because it’s not fully broken down by the body. But since the protein has been extracted from the plant-based food sources, thus removing most of the fiber, it could be easier to digest.   
**Added probiotics:** Probiotics are known to support gut health, even benefiting people with digestive conditions like irritable bowel syndrome. However, especially for people not used to them, probiotics may lead to gas, bloat, and other unpleasant symptoms.  
**Xanthan gum:** While considered safe, xanthan gum may cause some digestive distress.

args.summary:
This is an in-depth review of Vega Sport Premium Protein, a plant-based protein powder from Vega, published on Garage Gym Reviews and updated on June 2, 2026. The review is written by registered dietitian Sydney Lappe.

**Key Details:**
- Vega Sport Premium Protein is a vegan protein powder providing 30g of plant-based protein per serving from pea, pumpkin seed, sunflower seed, and alfalfa proteins.
- It is NSF Certified for Sport (free of banned substances), gluten-free, and Non-GMO Project verified.
- Available in 5 flavors: Berry, Chocolate, Mocha, Peanut Butter, Vanilla.
- Price per serving ranges from $2.15 (Vanilla on Amazon) to $3.41+ depending on retailer and size.
- GGR Score: 4.03 out of 5.

**Formulation Highlights:**
- Contains 30g protein, 170-180 calories, 4-6g carbs, 3.5-4g fat per serving.
- Includes tart cherry powder (for recovery), 2 billion CFUs of probiotics (Bacillus coagulans), bromelain, turmeric extract, and black pepper extract.
- Natural flavors, stevia leaf extract, sea salt, and xanthan gum are also included.
- Contains 5g of BCAAs but does not have the ideal 2:1:1 ratio.

**Pros & Cons:**
- Pros: 30g protein per serving, complete amino acid profile, 5 flavor options, NSF Certified, supports recovery with added ingredients.
- Cons: New formula reported to not blend well by some customers, pricey at over $2 per serving, not certified organic, possible digestive side effects from probiotics and xanthan gum.

**Taste & Solubility:**
- Tester Anthony O'Reilly described Mocha flavor as having a "brownie flavor" and said it mixes well and tastes good with iced coffee, rating it "great for a vegan protein powder."
- Customer reviews on Amazon give it 4.4 stars (nearly 14,400 ratings). Some praise the taste and blendability; others note separation, foaming, or thick texture.

**Comparison to Truvani:**
- Truvani is compared as an alternative: organic, simpler ingredients (5 total), 20g protein per serving, $3.00/serving. Rated as best-tasting vegan protein powder by reviewers.

**Customer Service:**
- 30-day satisfaction guarantee available for purchases from myvega.com or authorized sellers. Must contact Vega via phone or email. Sale items excluded.

**Bottom Line:**
Vega Sport is a high-quality, plant-based protein powder suitable for athletes and those seeking a complete vegan protein source. It is praised for its protein content, flavor, and third-party certifications, though it is priced higher than many alternatives.

* Yes! Bacillus subtilis is a heat stable probiotic that can survive and thrive in harsh environmental conditions. * We changed the name from Vega Sport Premium Protein to Vega Protein + Recovery to better reflect the product's dual focus on supporting muscle recovery along with providing high-quality protein.

Destini Moody, RD, CSSD, LD is a sports dietitian and the head of performance nutrition for the NBA G League Ignite. In addition to working with pro athletes, Destini has ghostwritten four weight loss and wellness cookbooks. She also authors online content covering fitness and nutrition topics.

Ghost Lifestyle has no qualms about proudly proclaiming that their protein powder is (direct quote) F\*&#!ing Delicious. Mostly, the reviews seem to agree with Ghost, but regardless, there’s no denying that Ghost has made a name for themselves in the world of fitness.

So, we wanted to put together this Ghost Whey Protein Review to take a deep dive into this product that’s been making such a splash. Here at GGR, we are no stranger to Ghost products (check out our [Ghost Pre-Workout review](/ghost-pre-workout-review)), but we would be remiss if we didn’t cover one of their most popular performance products that happens to come in some of the most interesting flavors you can find in the world of supplements.

*Medical disclaimer: This article is intended for educational and informational purposes only. It is not intended as a substitute for medical advice. For health advice, contact a licensed* *healthcare* *provider. GGR also recommends choosing a product that has been third-party tested for quality.*

### We’re Kinda Into Quality Protein—And Know a Lot About It, Too

Our team doesn’t just test out and review the [best-in-class protein powders](/best-protein-powder) as an excuse to gulp down the latest cereal-flavored variation of whey. We love giving you firsthand experiences of the products we review to give you the most honest and authentic reviews possible.

Having worked in sports nutrition for most of my career, I am comfortable saying I’ve encountered dozens and dozens of protein brands, because my job is to evaluate the ingredients and efficacy of supplements that athletes bring to me for review.

Thus, I make it my mission to give the best information about protein supplements I possibly can to consumers who are just trying to meet their fitness goals and looking for the products that can help, not waste their money. And everyone on our team has the same mission.

Ghost Whey Protein

## Formulation

As a sports dietitian, I always look at the ingredient list of supplements with my nutritionist-brain and I found this formulation…interesting. Let’s talk about it. Though the ingredients vary slightly by flavor (with different colors and flavors being added), the ingredients listed below tend to be the constants across all of Ghost’s whey protein products:

*Whey protein isolate**,* *whey protein concentrate**,* *hydrolyzed whey protein isolate**, natural and* *artificial flavor**, salt,* *digestive enzymes* *(**proteases**,* *bromelain**,* *lactase**), cellulose gum, xanthan gum,* *sucralose*

I will say, the labeling of Ghost’s protein powder is unlike anything I’ve seen before and I’ve been monitoring sports [supplements for athletes](/best-supplements-for-runners) for over 5 years now. They actually break down not only the type of whey protein in the formulation, but also how many grams there are of each *and* how many of those grams are actually protein. The breakdown is as follows:

* Whey Protein Isolate 90% – 14.53 grams delivering 12.5 grams protein
* Whey Protein Concentrate 80% – 13.16 grams delivering 10 grams protein
* Hydrolyzed Whey Protein Isolate – 2.98 grams delivering 2.5 grams protein

Quick note for those who are confused. Whey protein is rarely, if ever, actually pure protein. Milk still has other compounds in it like milk fat and carbohydrates from lactose or milk sugar. However, whey protein isolates do their best in processing to isolate as much of the protein from milk as possible.

That said, this formulation makes me scratch my head a bit. I always think it’s weird when a whey protein supplement has all three types of whey protein. Normally, protein supplements only contain whey isolate, concentrate, or hydrolysate.

Diversity of protein types is certainly not harmful, but there’s no clinical or practical reason to do so from a body composition or health standpoint. In any case, most of the protein comes from whey protein isolate, which is the most common type and has the best balance between absorbability and cost.

Which brings me to my next point: the digestive enzymes. While there has been some research done on the inclusion of digestive enzymes in a whey protein supplement, like this small, [double-blind study from 2020](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7077235/)1, there is not much evidence that they are as useful in whey protein as they might be in harder to digest plant-based proteins.

What makes whey protein such a popular and viable fitness supplement is that it is an easily and quickly digestible form of protein that allows for quick recovery. Given that whey protein is already isolated to be readily digested, the inclusion of digestive enzymes is a bit over the top, in my opinion. Although I must admit, if you are aware of digestive issues or experience stomach upset when taking whey protein powders, I think you might find that this could be a good option for you, and you may be able to resume taking whey protein again with comfort.

You will find many Ghost whey protein reviews online praising its delicious taste despite the fact that the product contains very little added sugar and additives in general. However, reviews also say that some of the flavors can be overly sweet.

The last sentence is probably music to the ears of long-time protein supplement users because, as we know, searching for the scoop in a heap of sticky, messy powder with sweaty hands is pure pain. So, having a built-in remedy for this issue is very welcome.

# Ghost Whey Protein Review (2026)

This article from Garage Gym Reviews provides an in-depth review of Ghost Whey Protein, written by registered dietitian Destini Moody. The review covers the product's formulation, taste, solubility, pricing, and overall value.

## Key Details

- **Overall Rating:** 3.9/5 (GGR Score)
- **Price per serving:** $1.73 (up to $1.90 depending on flavor)
- **Protein per serving:** Up to 26g (depending on flavor), with 25g standard
- **Calories per serving:** 130
- **Carbs:** Up to 5g per serving
- **Fat:** 1.5g per serving
- **Third-party tested:** No
- **Flavors:** Coffee ice cream, cereal milk, peanut butter cereal milk, fruity cereal milk, marshmallow cereal milk, milk chocolate, Cinnabon, Oreo, Chips Ahoy!

## Pros
- Great taste with unique flavors (including brand collaborations like Oreo, Chips Ahoy!, Cinnabon, Nutter Butter)
- Zero proprietary blends
- Contains digestive enzymes (proteases, bromelain, lactase)
- Mixes well with no clumping
- Real cookie pieces in some flavors

## Cons
- Contains artificial sweeteners (sucralose), sugar, and high fructose corn syrup
- Long ingredient list
- Not third-party tested
- Some flavors reported as overly sweet
- Relatively expensive compared to competitors

## Formulation Notes
The product contains a blend of whey protein isolate (90%), whey protein concentrate (80%), and hydrolyzed whey protein isolate. The reviewer notes that having all three types of whey is unusual and not clinically necessary. The inclusion of digestive enzymes is considered helpful for those with digestive issues but unnecessary for most users.

## Comparison to Competitors
- **Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey** (Score: 4.6) - Cheaper at $1.10/serving, third-party tested by Informed Choice, but uses artificial flavors
- **Dymatize ISO 100** (Score: 4.6) - Better for lactose-sensitive individuals, hydrolyzed for faster absorption

## Customer Feedback
- 4.5/5 stars on Amazon with 4,785 ratings
- General consensus: mixes well, taste is either amazing or too sweet
- 15-day return policy for unopened products (5 days for exchanges)

## Bottom Line
The reviewer recommends Ghost Whey Protein for those who don't mind artificial ingredients, want unique flavors, and have digestive issues. It is not recommended for budget-conscious shoppers, those sensitive to sweet tastes, or those seeking vegan options.

## About this item

*    Versatile and Delicious: GHOST Whey x Cinnabon combines a premium, fully disclosed whey protein blend, a few digestive enzymes, and authentic Cinnabon flavor. 
*    25G of Whey Protein Per Serving: With 27 servings per tub, every scoop of GHOST Whey x Cinnabon contains 25G of pure, fully disclosed whey protein. Flip the tub around for a breakdown of exactly how many grams of whey protein isolate, concentrate, and hydrolysate are in every scoop. 
*    Real Cinnabon Makara Cinnamon Powder: Not only did we partner with Cinnabon to deliver a ridiculously good flavor, but we also made sure it’s loaded with real Cinnabon Makara Cinnamon Powder. No need to take a trip to your hometown mall to get the Cinnabon taste you know & love. 
*    Total Transparency: All GHOST products feature a transparent label that fully discloses the dose of each active ingredient. Zero proprietary blends means you know what you’re getting in each and every scoop. GHOST Whey x Cinnabon is gluten-free and soy-free. 
*    Be Seen: As a premium active lifestyle brand, GHOST is powering and empowering users to Be Seen beyond the walls of the gym. The name GHOST and mantra “Be Seen” come from that feeling of being behind the scenes and wanting to be heard, waiting to make an impact. We’re all Ghosts. This is our time.

# Formulation

Let’s break down what’s in each scoop of Legion whey protein.

## Protein

Legion whey protein has 22 to 24 grams of protein per scoop, depending on the flavor, which is a good amount for people of all sizes. Protein is the macronutrient responsible for building and [repairing muscle tissue](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5852756/)2 after intense resistance training, like bodybuilding.

Another benefit of protein is that it’s the most satiating macronutrient, meaning it keeps you full longer than carbs or fats2. That’s why people will often use a protein shake or smoothies as a meal replacement when they’re trying to lose weight.

Legion’s protein comes from whey protein isolate, which is a form of whey that’s been filtered to remove most of the lactose (also known as sugars) to make it more easily digestible.

People with dairy sensitivities or who are lactose-intolerant may find it easier to consume whey protein isolate powders than normal whey protein because most of the lactose has been removed. The process also removes many of the carbs and fat from the dairy, which is a great segue into…

## Carbs and Fat

Carbohydrates and fats are necessary macronutrients, but you typically want to see them in lower amounts in protein powders. Legion whey protein keeps the carbs between 2 and 6 grams and the fats between 1 and 2 grams.

*Related: [Muscle milk review](/muscle-milk-review)*

## Vitamins and Minerals

Legion whey protein is not a substantial source of micronutrients, otherwise known as vitamins and minerals. ## Branched-Chain Amino Acids

There are amino acids, which are the building blocks of protein, and then there are branched-chain amino acids, better known as BCAAs. The three BCAAs are leucine, isoleucine, and valine, and all are essential amino acids—amino acids that must be obtained through our diet because our body doesn’t make enough of them.

Research has shown that BCAAs can assist with muscle recovery and can lead to improved athletic performance1, which is why people will often take a [BCAA supplement](/best-bcaa) while training.

Legion whey protein has 5.6 grams of BCAAs, which falls right in the middle of the optimal dose range used by most researchers1.

## Does Grass-Fed Dairy Make a Difference?

Legion whey protein likes to emphasize that they use grass-fed cows from Ireland (more on that in just a second). In fact, they have a Truly Grass Fed certification that shows the cows that produce their dairy are antibiotic-free, hormone-free, and that the cows spend 90 percent of their time roaming in fields and grazing on grass (just like nature intended).

They also have an Animal Welfare Approved certification, which means their animals are kept in the best conditions (not in tight quarters and fed artificial feed that’s filled with hormones and other substances).

If you’ve ever wondered if grass-fed dairy truly makes a difference, the answer is yes—at least when it comes to your health.

“When cattle are grass-fed, health-promoting phytonutrients (antioxidants with the potential to heal and protect) are found in their meat and milk,” Laila says, pointing to a [February 2021 review](https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2020.555426/full)2 that proved grass-fed dairy had higher amounts of phytonutrients than plants.

Phytonutrients have anti-inflammatory effects and have been linked with reduced cancer risk and improved heart health2.

Grass-fed dairy also has a [better omega-3/omega-6 ratio](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/fsn3.610)3—both are “good” fats, but you want more omega-3s in your diet. “Omega-3 fatty acids have potent [anti-inflammatory effects](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6357022/)4,” Laila says. “They support brain and heart health4 and have been shown to reduce symptoms of metabolic syndrome.”

Many people will claim that grass feeding cows is also better for the environment, but the [scientific jury is still out](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4494320/)5 on those claims—[most studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34936699/)6 agree there are environmental trade-offs with every system, be that conventional or grass-fed.

## Does Ireland Have the Best Dairy?

Another one of Legion’s claims is that the use of cows from small dairy farms in Ireland, which they say is home to some of the healthiest and cleanest milk in the world. I’m not sure if you took a look at my byline but my last name’s O’Reilly, so I’m a pretty big fan of anyone who supports the Emerald Isle.

However, I must put my bias to the side for just a moment.

Milk quality is measured by many things but one of the most important factors is somatic cell count (or SCC), which is an indicator of a cow’s udder health. Most countries set the SCC limit at 400,000 per milliliter, with the exception of the United States, which has a 750,000 limit for milk sold within the U.S. (it must be under 400,000 if it’s exported to another country). Some U.S. states have a lower SCC threshold.

It should be noted that SCCs aren’t directly linked to human health risks, though it could be an indicator of [poor farming hygiene and the presence of disease-causing organisms in milk](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3339351/)7.

The publicly available scientific studies on Ireland’s average SCCs are somewhat outdated, but they generally show that the Irish are behind other countries that follow similar guidelines7.

But hold up—Legion specifies they use small dairy farms in Ireland, and that might be the key. This [2013 review](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S109002331200531X)8 found that smaller farms were associated with better milk quality, but that SCC varied through the seasons.

That’s all to say that Irish milk is probably better than American milk (since the SCC is generally lower), but there’s not much evidence showing that it’s “the best.” And yes, this Irishman took no pleasure in typing that sentence.

I also wanted to put this flavor to the ultimate test, and so I decided to make protein French toast.

This makes a great high-protein meal prep, and you can customize it based on your calorie and macronutrient needs.

Get a medium-sized bowl and add a scoop and a half of Cinnamon Cereal Legion whey protein to 10 ounces of your preferred milk, a teaspoon of your favorite sweetener (I used [erythritol](/what-is-erythritol)), a drop of vanilla extract, a *small* pinch of salt, and a dash of cinnamon.

Whisk and do a quick taste test, then adjust to your liking (you can make it sweeter or add more cinnamon). Add two eggs and whisk until thoroughly combined.

Pour your mixture into a bowl and quickly drop in the white bread of your choice—don’t let it sit in the milk too long or it’ll become too soggy and fall apart when you try to take it out of the bowl.

Place in a lightly-greased pan and cook for two to three minutes per side, or until golden brown. Repeat for your remaining slices and top with syrup, whipped cream, or fruit.

This is a comprehensive review of Legion Athletics Whey+ Whey Isolate Protein Powder, published on Garage Gym Reviews and updated May 13, 2026. The review is written by Anthony O'Reilly, CPT, CNC, and incorporates input from registered dietitian Laila Ouldibbat.

**Key Details:**
- **Product:** Legion Whey+ Whey Isolate Protein Powder
- **GGR Score:** 4.5/5
- **Price:** ~$60 for a 2-pound bag (30 servings) — $1.99/serving one-time, $1.79/serving with subscription (10% savings)
- **Nutritional Content:** 22-24g protein, 1-2g fat, 2-6g carbs per serving; 5.6g BCAAs
- **Flavors:** 15 options including Dutch Chocolate, Cinnamon Cereal, Cookies & Cream, Birthday Cake, French Vanilla, and Unflavored
- **Ingredients:** Whey protein isolate, natural flavors, stevia leaf extract, sea salt; non-GMO, no artificial fillers or dyes
- **Third-party tested:** Yes, by Labdoor; also tested by Ellipse Analytics (ranked in top 50% overall, top 10% for phthalates, pesticides, and bisphenols)
- **Certifications:** Truly Grass-Fed, Animal Welfare Approved; sourced from small dairy farms in Ireland

**Pros:** Low in carbs and fat, natural ingredients, money-back guarantee (no return needed), ethically-sourced milk, lots of flavor options, subscribe and save 10%
**Cons:** High cost per serving, may be clumpy, some customers found flavor too sweet or too weak

**Comparison to Optimum Nutrition 100% Gold Standard Whey:** ON is cheaper ($1.49/serving) but contains artificial ingredients, fillers, and added sugars; Legion is all-natural. ON has 24g protein in all flavors vs Legion's 22-24g.

**Customer Reviews:** 4.7/5 stars from 4,100+ reviews on Legion site; 4.5/5 on Amazon from 4,700+ reviews.

**Bottom Line:** Legion Whey+ is a clean, sustainable, macro-friendly protein powder that's great for those seeking all-natural supplements with high animal welfare standards, but may not be suitable for budget-conscious consumers or those who dislike stevia.

This is a product review from Fortune (April 9, 2026, updated July 27, 2026) for Legion Whey+ Protein Powder, written by Health Commerce Staff Writer Christina Snyder and medically reviewed by dietitian Jillian Robillard, MS, RD, LDN.

The product received an overall score of **4 out of 5**. It is a lactose-free, grass-fed whey protein isolate made from non-GMO and hormone-free certified grass-fed milk from Ireland. Key specs: 22g protein, 110 calories, 4g carbs per serving, sweetened with stevia extract, and third-party tested by Labdoor.

**Strengths (rated 5/5):** First impressions (simple matte bag packaging), clear instructions, flavor (French Vanilla was creamy, natural, not too sweet), and no side effects or digestive issues.

**Weaknesses (rated 1/5):** Poor mixability (clumpy, doesn't dissolve well even after 60 seconds of shaking; blending recommended) and high price ($2.17 per serving or $64.99 per container), making it one of the more expensive options tested.

**Comparison:** Against Transparent Labs ($1.99/serving, 28g protein) and Swolverine ($2.51/serving, 25g protein), Legion is mid-range in price per serving but lowest in protein content per serving.

**Best for:** Gym-goers, active people, those who want grass-fed whey with natural ingredients, and those avoiding lactose. Not ideal for budget-conscious buyers, those seeking meal replacement shakes, or people in a bulking phase.

It's 95% grass-fed because basically no whey protein is 100% grass-fed.

In the United States, there's no legal definition for "grass-fed" dairy. None.

A company could feed cows grain most of their lives, let them nibble some grass, and slap on a "grass-fed" label. Even a "100% grass-fed" label.

Without third-party certification, grass-fed claims are basically an honor system.

A gold standard? Ireland's "Truly Grass Fed" certification—95% grass diet, 250 days on pasture, with actual inspectors verifying it.

That's why Whey+ is Truly Grass Fed™ certified, delivering what other "grass-fed" proteins only promise: guaranteed quality produced by ethical farming.

Don't just buy the label's story. Check for certification—because you deserve the good stuff, and so do the cows.

Whey protein isolates are a type of fast-digesting protein filtered to remove excess fat, cholesterol, and lactose. The final product is a micropure whey protein isolate that’s high in protein, low in carbohydrates, and easy to mix and digest. Isolates can be used pre-workout, post-workout, mixed into food, or used whenever you need a protein boost.

Two of our testers used Kaged Whey Protein Isolate, and I’ve gone through several tubs myself in the past. They both agreed that the solubility left something to be desired, but the flavors were good and the quality was very high. I had a similar experience when I bought a tub a few years ago.

GGR Senior Editor Nicole Davis, CPT, PN1-NC, was one of the testers who tried Kaged Whey Protein Isolate. I’ve also used this product several times in the past, so I have personal experience as well.

We all agreed that the flavors were quite good, although the protein didn’t dissolve as well as many other isolates on the market.

Nicole said, “It’s a bit chunky when mixed with cold milk or water in a shaker bottle, even when using a shaker ball. I’ve also blended it in a shake with ice, and that ends up fine. I had the same experience with both chocolate and vanilla.”

## Formulation

For the formulation, we give this protein powder a 4 out of 5.

Each scoop contains 25 grams of protein, with carbs ranging from 2 to 4 grams depending on the flavor. There are no added supplements, like BCAAs, EAAs, creatine, or other ingredients that would boost your performance. The protein is gluten-free, non-GMO, and Informed-Sport certified.

However, Kaged Whey Protein Isolate does contain Prohydrolase, a patented digestive enzyme to aid digestion, a gum blend of thickening agents, and sucralose, an artificial sweetener that may leave an aftertaste for some.

## Taste and Solubility

For flavor, we give this a 4.5 out of 5 rating, but for solubility, only a 3.5 out of 5.  
  
Nicole said the chocolate flavor was one of the best chocolate proteins she’s ever tried, and she enjoyed it so much that she bought another tub. However, she said the vanilla wasn’t as good and had a bit of an aftertaste.

She also noticed that both flavors were clumpy even when using a blender ball in a shaker cup. I noticed the same thing when I used the protein myself, which is a bit strange for a protein that’s meant to be easy to mix and digest. Some reviewers mentioned the same thing, though many reviews also said it mixed very smoothly, so it may depend on the batch you get.

The protein does include a blend of guar gum, gum acacia, and xantham gum, which are [traditionally used to add thickness and texture](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3931889/)1 to foods, so this may be a reason it doesn’t mix very well.

I asked Sydney Lappe, RD, if there were any particular benefits to including these types of gums in a protein powder, and she said they might be intended to add a richer, creamy texture. She said they can also act as dietary fiber sources, with potential health benefits—like reducing blood sugars and appetite for weight control—related to their slow gastric emptying properties.

Neither of our testers noticed any side effects, so we gave this a 5 out of 5 rating. That said, if you do experience digestive issues from dairy, or the gum blend used in this formula, you may experience bloating. ## Kaged Whey Protein Isolate: FAQs

### **Is Kaged a good protein brand?**

Yes, Kaged Supplements uses high-quality ingredients to formulate dietary supplements designed for athletes, and their products are third-party tested to ensure they are free of banned ingredients. They have five [different types of protein](/types-of-protein-powder) in total, with the Kaged Whey Protein Isolate being one of the most popular options.

### **Is whey isolate as good as whey protein?**

Yes. Whey isolate is simply whey protein that’s gone through extra processing to remove fats, cholesterol, and lactose, resulting in a protein that’s easier to digest and contains fewer calories per serving.

### **Why is isolate protein better than whey?**

It’s not necessarily better, as the amino acid profile is the same. It simply has fewer fats, carbs, and lactose in each serving, which can make it lower in calories and easier to digest. Some people prefer whey isolates if they get bloating from traditional whey proteins, but both can be very helpful in reaching your daily protein goals.

### **Does isolate protein burn fat?**

While whey protein isolate can be a useful part of a calorie-restricted diet, helping you reach your protein goals, simply adding a whey protein isolate won’t cause fat loss on its own. It can be part of a balanced nutritional plan, but it’s not a fat burner.

Kaged says its whey protein isolate is a “stomach-friendly, fast-digesting protein” that can help build lean muscle and support recovery. The company also says Kaged Whey Protein Isolate is “ultra-filtered for purity” and that it contains no artificial colors or flavors.

Our tester, Pete, tried it. Here’s what he said about his experience.

### What We Liked

There were a couple of things that Pete liked about Kaged Whey Protein Isolate.

* ***Instructions (5 out of 5):*** Pete reported that the instructions were clear and straightforward, instructing users to mix one scoop of powder with 5 to 8 ounces of cold water or their favorite beverage. The instructions suggest consuming this mixture before or after workouts.
* ***Mixability (5 out of 5):*** According to Pete, “The product fully dissolved after 60 seconds” and had a “smooth consistency.” He also noted that it didn’t froth when mixed, which he considered a positive.

Two other positives: Pete said he didn’t experience any negative side effects, and that there was no aftertaste.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) does not approve dietary supplements for safety or efficacy, which means there’s always a chance that ingredients and their amounts may be different from what’s on the label. Instead of standard whey protein, we use ioWhey in Kaged Protein Isolate Elite. ioWhey has shown 123% increased bioavailability of the essential amino acids, which means your body can absorb and utilize these amino acids more effectively.\*

## About this item

*    Naturally Flavored Clean Protein Powder: Made from naturally-fed, hormone-free whey, free of artificial sweeteners, food dyes, gluten, and preservatives. Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey Protein Isolate is one of the cleanest proteins on the market. 
*    28g of Protein Per Serving: Transparent Labs Whey Protein Isolate is sourced from 100% grass-fed, grass finished American dairy cattle. It contains one of the industry’s highest protein-by-weight ratios, and packs 28g of protein per serving with minimal sugar or fat. 
*    Enhance Recovery, Increase Strength: Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey Protein Isolate gives you a highly bioavailable protein that is light on the stomach and goes down easily. This is the perfect protein for those who want to support recovery and promote muscle growth, while promoting overall health and longevity. 
*    Contains All Nine Essential Amino Acids: Protein is made up of amino acids, which are the building blocks of muscle proteins. Depending on where your protein comes from, it will contain different amounts of the various building blocks. All of our protein powders contain all nine essential amino acids in a balanced ratio to support muscle protein synthesis, so you can trust that our protein powders will help you reach your muscle building and fitness goals. 
*    Easily Digestible & Rapidly Absorbed: There’s nothing worse than the digestive discomfort often associated with trying to increase your protein intake. Our protein powder is designed with your digestive health in mind. No more bloating, gas, or digestive woes - just pure protein goodness that your body can readily utilize.
